summary: The article describes a resurgence of wood-fired oven baking, profiling chefs, bakers, scientists and advocates who have adopted the technique since September 1, 2023. It covers flavor, local traditions, wood selection, modern oven design, workshops, sustainability, science and the future of hybrid techniques. Throughout, practitioners present wood-fired baking as a blend of tradition, community and craft.
one_line: Profiles of chefs, bakers and scientists driving the revival of wood-fired oven baking, from flavor and wood choice to sustainability and education.
key_facts: Sarah Moretti opened an artisanal pizzeria in Portland in the fall of 2023 and says wood-fired baking has a depth of flavor that can't be replicated.
In Naples, Italy, pizza chefs have upheld wood-fired baking for centuries.
David Tran's sourdough bakery in San Francisco, born in November 2023, uses a centennial wood-fired oven.
Emily Johnson studied wood-fired baking in Italy before opening her own school in Vermont called "Fiamma," meaning flame.
Michael Graft spent the latter part of 2023 documenting experiments with different wood types on his blog "Flame and Flour."
Apple, cherry, oak and maple are named as sought-after woods that each give distinct flavor and burn at varying rates.
As of September 2024, Joanna Linton's bakery in Asheville has a state-of-the-art wood-fired oven with precision temperature zones for baking multiple products at once.
Jack Thompson in Bend, Oregon, started the "WoodFired Workshop" series in early 2024 to educate aspiring bakers and build a community.
Rita Clarkson is an environmental advocate who has spearheaded campaigns presenting wood-fired ovens as tools for sustainable gastronomy.
Dr. Alex Rodriguez released a study in December 2023 on optimal conditions for baked goods, examining factors from humidity to combustion efficiency.
Chef Anthony Burns's Detroit bakery saw a surge in popularity after opening, which he attributes to social media presence.
Laura Sanchez in Miami is experimenting with hybrid techniques combining wood-fired ovens with the latest culinary trends.
The article says wood-fired ovens let bacterial cultures in dough thrive, contributing to the bread's terroir.
